cape.why: THE STORED SINGULAR IS A VERB. SAOL: 'kapa verb ~de ~t' = to saw/chop off; to hijack. There is NO noun kapa — the singular field holds a verb, and the script then pluralised it into the equally non-existent *Kapor. The correct noun is SAOL's 'cape [kä´p] substantiv ~n [-en]; pl. ~r [-er]', defined as 'ett ärmlöst plagg som läggs över axlarna' = a SLEEVELESS garment laid over the shoulders — which is the picture, word for word. I considered the alternative that Kapa is a typo for kappa (a coat; SAOL 'kappa ~n kappor'), but the picture rules that out: a kappa has sleeves and this garment has none. The picture is what settles it.

muffin.why: 'Muffin' IS NOT A SWEDISH WORD. SAOL: 'Inga träffar på muffin. Menade du muffins, mufflon eller muff?'. The Swedish borrowing took the English PLURAL as its SINGULAR: SO gives 'muffins muffinsen, plural muffins el. muffinsar' and SAOL 'muffins ~en hellre än ~et; pl. ~ hellre än ~ar' — i.e. EN MUFFINS, flera muffins. The data imported the English singular/plural pair wholesale. Same lexeme, wrong form -> FIX.

pegasus.why: 'Pegasus' is not the Swedish word. SAOL does not contain it and suggests 'pegas'; the entry is 'pegas [pega´s] substantiv ~en ~er — bevingad häst som symbol för diktkonsten', and SO gives 'pegas pegasen pegaser — ett mytologiskt, bevingat hästdjur'. Pegas is the naturalised Swedish common noun. ⚠ SEPARATE ART FINDING for the operator: the picture has a HORN, so strictly it is not a pegas in ANY language — a picture/classification question affecting all 11 locales, not a Swedish form defect. The form fix stands however the art question is ruled.

air-conditioning.why: SAOL: "luft|konditionering substantiv ~en ~ar" -> plural luftkonditioneringar. The stored zero-plural is wrong; the word DOES inflect. This agrees with classification hasPlural:true (and contradicts the row own countable:false).

ankle.why: SAOL: "vrist substantiv ~en ~er" -> plural VRISTER. "Vristar" is the script -ar default swallowing a 3rd-declension noun (the ambulans/antilop/paj class the brief names).

asparagus.why: SAOL: "sparr·is substantiv ~en ~ar" -> plural SPARRISAR. The stored zero-plural is wrong. The brief itself warns that _countable:false is fallible and names asparagus as one of the words that DOES have a real plural — SAOL confirms it, and classification hasPlural:true agrees (the row own countable:false is the wrong field).

baby.why: SO: "baby babyn, plural BABIES el. BABYS". SAOL gives only ~n (no -ar plural anywhere). "Babyar" is invented by the script -ar default. English loans take -s, not -ar (cf. bagel->bagels, body->bodies in this same batch). Babies is first-listed; Babys is the sanctioned alternative if the operator prefers the Swedish-looking spelling.

baby's-onesie.why: SAOL: "body substantiv ~n; pl. BODIES" -> babybody->babybodies. "Babybodyar" is the script -ar default; same English-loan -s class as baby->babies and bagel->bagels.

bagel.why: SAOL: "bagel [bej´gel] substantiv ~n; pl. ~S" -> BAGELS. SO agrees ("bagel bageln bagels"). "Baglar" is the script wrongly applying -el syncope (as in nyckel->nycklar) to an English loan; English loans take -s (cf. baby->babies, body->bodies in this batch).

boombox.why: 'Bärbar stereoar' is wrong TWICE. (1) Noun: SAOL '1stereo substantiv ~n ~r / stereoanläggning' → the plural is stereor, not *stereoar — the script's default -ar. (2) Adjective: an indefinite plural attributive takes -a → bärbara, not the uninflected bärbar. The same construction is done correctly one row away at boiled-egg (Kokt ägg → Kokta ägg), which is what proves this is a defect and not a convention.

cape.why: SAOL 'cape substantiv ~n; pl. ~r' and SO 'cape capen caper' → Caper. The stored *Kapor is the script's -a→-or plural of a verb; it is not a Swedish word.

chili-pepper.why: 'Chilipepprar' is an invented form — the script's half-written -ar/syncope rule fired on a mass noun. SAOL gives 'chili|peppar ~n' with NO plural form at all; SO gives only 'chilipeppar chilipepparn'. Same for the short form: SAOL 'chili ~n', no plural. This contradicts the row's classification (countable-thing / hasPlural:true) — but there is no image here, so the classifier had nothing to see, and the dictionary wins. For countable fruit Swedish says chilifrukter or chilis, never *chilipepprar.

dogwood-tree.why: SAOL: korn·ell substantiv ~en ~er ⇒ korneller. SO: 'kornell kornellen korneller'. 3rd declension. 'Kornellar' is the script's -ar default and does not exist.

dresser.why: HOMOGRAPH TRAP — the data took the WRONG one of two SAOL entries. SAOL: 1byrå substantiv ~n ~ar = 'en möbel' ⇒ byråar; 2byrå substantiv ~n ~er = 'avdelning av ämbetsverk e.d.; kontor, mottagning; företag' ⇒ byråer. The picture is the FURNITURE (1byrå), so the plural must be byråar. The stored 'Byråer' is the OFFICE plural — a correct Swedish word attached to the wrong sense. Exactly the bok→bokar (tree) / böcker (book) class the brief warns about, and only the picture settles it.

durian.why: SAOL: durian [du´-] substantiv ~en ~er ⇒ durianer. 3rd declension. 'Durianar' is the script's -ar default and does not exist.

forget-me-not.why: 'Förgätmigejar' is sanctioned by NEITHER authority — the script's default -ar again. SAOL: 'förgätmigej ~en; pl. ~ el. ~er'. SO: 'plural förgätmigej el. förgätmigejer'. Both give zero OR -er; -ar is not an option. I give the overt -er form because a zero plural is useless as a spoken plural label beside a picture; SAOL lists zero first, so 'Förgätmigej' would also be defensible. This fix stands regardless of how the picture question is resolved, as long as the lemma stays.

garden-fork.why: The stored zero plural is wrong. The head noun 'grep' is a common-gender monosyllable taking -ar: grep → grepen → grepar → greparna. Zero plural is the ETT-word consonant-final pattern; 'grep' is an EN-word (as the data itself codes it, g='n'), so it cannot take it. SAOL's 'grep' entry sits behind a six-way disambiguation page the fetch tool cannot resolve past, and SAOL has no 'trädgårdsgrep' compound entry (normal — Swedish compounds freely), so I cite the sv.wiktionary paradigm via --crosscheck rather than fabricate a SAOL citation. Flagging that this rests on a cross-check source plus the declension rule, not on SAOL directly.
garden-fork.src: https://sv.wiktionary.org/wiki/grep (via dict-fetch --crosscheck; paradigm grep · grepen · grepar · greparna, 'grep u')

gecko.why: SAOL: 'gecko [gek´o] substantiv ~n ~r' → geckor. SO confirms: 'gecko geckon geckor'. The stored 'Geckos' is an English plural imported wholesale; it appears in neither authority. Contrast frisbee in this same batch, where SO DOES list the -s form — hence OK there and FIX here. The -s ending is not uniformly right or wrong for loans; it has to be looked up word by word.

hemlock-tree.why: The stored zero plural is wrong. SAOL gives '~en ~ar' explicitly and SO confirms 'hemlock hemlocken hemlockar'. Nets N2/N8/N4 are right to flag this one. A zero plural would require an ett-word; hemlock is an en-word (~en), as the data itself codes it (g='n') — the two fields contradict each other, and the gender field is the one that is right. This fix stands independently of the art question above. (The superseded verdicts file HELD this as unverifiable and separately claimed the gender read 't' and needed fixing; the dictionary settles the plural outright, and the gender is already 'n'.)

hospital-gown.why: 'Sjukhuskläderar' does not exist — it is the script's -ar default bolted onto an already-plural noun, exactly the brief's Gardinerar/Musklerar class. kläder is plural already; the indefinite plural is 'sjukhuskläder' (def. pl. sjukhuskläderna). Removing the invented form is right whichever way the lemma question is settled.

iguanodon.why: LOWER-CONFIDENCE, PATTERN-BASED — saying so plainly rather than faking a citation: iguanodon is in NEITHER SAOL, SO nor SAOB (verified), so the -ar here is the script's unmotivated default. Crucially this is NOT the -us class: the Latin rule that justifies Ichthyosaurusar (kaktus→kaktusar) does not reach a word ending in -on. The attested Swedish pattern for utrum nouns in stressed -on is -er: SAOL 'elektron ~en ~er' → elektroner (likewise proton/neutron/melon). Applying each ending its own attested rule gives Iguanodoner. Operator may prefer to leave it pending a native/palaeontology-usage check.

jam.why: THE DICTIONARY DECIDES: SAOL 'sylt ~en ~er' and SO 'sylt sylten sylter' both give a real plural, and classification independently says countable-thing/hasPlural:true — so the identical singular/plural wrongly encodes 'no plural'. This is precisely the brief's inverse trap in reverse ('_countable is fallible — wrong on bread, asparagus, cheese...'): sylt does pluralise (kinds of jam), so calling it a mass noun and leaving p=s is not defensible against SAOL.

juice.why: THE DICTIONARY DECIDES: SAOL 'juice ~n [jo´sen]; pl. ~r [jo`ser]' → juicer, and SO 'juice juicen juicer'. Both give the plural outright, and classification says countable-thing/hasPlural:true — so the identical singular/plural wrongly encodes 'no plural'. Treating juice as an uncountable mass noun is an English intuition that SAOL does not share.

kettlebell.why: IT IS IN SAOL — no need to hold: 'kettlebell [ket´elbel] substantiv ~en; pl. ~s'. SAOL gives ONLY -s. 'Kettlebellar' is the script's -ar default and is not a Swedish form. This is the batch-01 lesson ('EN loans take -s not -ar') and SAOL confirms it outright for this word.

keyboard.why: IT IS IN SAOL — no need to hold, and the result is COUNTER-INTUITIVE: 'keyboard ~en el. ~et; pl. ~ar el. ~' gives keyboardar OR zero, and does NOT list *keyboards. So the batch-01 'EN loans take -s' heuristic does NOT hold for this word — keyboard is a nativised loan, unlike kettlebell in this same batch where SAOL gives ~s only. That contrast is exactly why each loan must be looked up rather than ruled by class. Taking SAOL's first-listed form: Keyboardar (zero plural 'Keyboard' would also be sanctioned).

lavender.why: THE DICTIONARY BEATS THE CLASSIFICATION HERE: classification says hasPlural:true, but SAOL gives 'lavendel ~n' with NO plural form at all, and SO gives only 'lavendel lavendeln'. SAOL does list plurals when they exist — contrast 'nyckel ~n nycklar' in this same batch — so the omission is meaningful: lavendel is treated as a mass/substance plant name. Noting fairly that the current 'Lavendlar' is at least morphologically well formed (the -el syncope is right), so that is the shape it would take if a plural were ever forced; but no authority sanctions it.

lime.why: SAOL 'lime [laj´m] substantiv ~n [-en]; pl. ~r [-er]' → LIMER, and SO confirms outright: 'lime limen limer'. 'Limar' is the script's -ar default and is not a Swedish form — lime ends in an unstressed -e, so it takes 2nd-declension -r, not -ar.

parasaurolophus.why: A zero plural is wrong for this class and is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT with its two siblings in this same batch (Pachycephalosaurusar, Plesiosaurusar). Latin -us loans take -ar, verified on the attested class member: SAOL 'kakt·us substantiv ~en ~ar'. Pure form correction of the same word.

pegasus.why: The stored zero plural is wrong under either lemma. SAOL 'pegas ~en ~er'; SO gives the paradigm outright: 'pegas pegasen pegaser'.

persimmon.why: The script's default -ar is wrong; this is a 3rd-declension -er noun. SAOL: 'persimon [-må´n] substantiv ~en ~er'. Exactly the class the brief says the builder swallowed (ambulans→ambulanser, antilop→antiloper).

phlox.why: ⚠ CONTRADICTS the classification (hasPlural: true) — and the dictionary wins. BOTH authorities give a singular-only paradigm: SAOL 'flox ~en' (gender only, no plural listed) and SO 'flox floxen' (singular + definite singular, no plural). The stored 'Floxar' is therefore unattested — an invented form of exactly the kind this commission exists to delete. I deliberately do NOT propose a replacement plural: inventing one is the defect. The honest state is 'no established plural', the word being used collectively for the garden plant. Ran --crosscheck; sv.wiktionary returned 404, so it adds nothing either way.

pickup-truck.why: SAOL gives '~er', not the script's default -ar. This cuts BOTH against the stored -ar AND against the brief's 'EN loans take -s not -ar' guidance: the dictionary gives a third answer, and it wins. Contrast 'pyjamas' in this batch, where SAOL genuinely gives -ar — English loans follow no single rule; each must be looked up.

squash.why: RESOLVES the v1 'needs a SAOL lookup' HOLD. SAOL: '2squash ... substantiv ~en ~er' → the plural is squasher (3rd declension -er), NOT *squashar. The stored 'Squashar' is the documented default -ar that swallows the whole 3rd declension (cf. ambulans→ambulanser, antilop→antiloper, paj→pajer) — v1's suspicion that the -ar had 'fired by luck rather than by rule' is confirmed. Pure form correction of the same word.

suv.why: SAOL: 'suv [su´v el. suv´] substantiv ~en ~ar' → plural 'suvar', with NO colon. The colon convention is decided PER WORD by SAOL, not by a blanket initialism rule: SAOL DOES write 'tv ~:n ~:ar' with colons, but writes plain '~en ~ar' for suv and '~t ~n' for ufo. So a Svenska-skrivregler-style appeal to the initialism rule is overridden by SAOL's own lexicalised entry, and per the brief the dictionary wins. 'SUV:ar' is additionally a text-to-speech hazard on a site that reads the word aloud to 3-7-year-olds.

tape.why: SAOL 'tejp substantiv ~en ~er' → tejper. The stored zero plural 'Tejp' is not a SAOL form, and the row is classified countable-thing/hasPlural:true, so a plural is required.

taxi.why: BOTH authorities decline to give a -er plural and BOTH name taxibilar instead. SAOL: 'taxi [tak´si] substantiv ~n, i pl. används vanl. taxibilar'. SO: 'taxi taxin; som plural kan användas taxibilar'. 'Taxier' is therefore unsupported — it is the script's -er default. Taxibilar is the form the dictionaries actually give, and SAOL+SO agreeing makes this a solid fix rather than a judgement call.
taxi.src: https://svenska.se/saol/?sok=taxi (SAOL entry; the SO entry renders on https://svenska.se/tre/?sok=taxi)

timer.why: SAOL: 'timer [taj´mer] substantiv ~n; pl. ~' — the plural is ZERO (en timer → flera timer). The stored 'Timrar' is the script's -el/-er syncope rule (nyckel→nycklar, hummer→humrar) misapplied to an English loan that SAOL does not syncopate at all. This is a manufactured non-word of exactly the Gardinerar / Musklerar class the commission exists to delete. Independent of the singular HOLD: whatever the lemma, 'Timrar' is not a Swedish form of 'timer'.

triceratops.why: SAOL has NO entry ('Inga träffar på triceratops. Menade du triceps eller triumfator?' — stated, not fabricated). The only lexicographic source that carries it, sv.wiktionary, gives the utrum declension: triceratops / triceratopsen / TRICERATOPSER / triceratopserna. The stored 'Triceratopsar' presupposes the Latin -us→-ar loan rule (kaktusar, Stegosaurusar) — but triceratops does not end in Latin -us; it ends in Greek -ops (ὤψ), so that rule does not license it. CONFIDENCE NOTE: this rests on ONE Wiktionary edition (en.wiktionary has no Swedish section for it), which by the brief's own standard is not conclusive; surfaced as the best-supported form rather than leaving an unsourced script guess standing. Worth a second native opinion.

ufo.why: SAOL: 'ufo [u´fo] substantiv ~t ~n' → plural 'ufon', with NO colon. SAOL treats ufo as a fully lexicalised ordinary ett-word, not as an initialism — contrast its OWN entry for tv, which it writes 'tv ~:n ~:ar' WITH colons. So the colon convention is decided per word by SAOL, and for ufo it says no. 'UFO:n' is additionally a text-to-speech hazard on a site that reads the word aloud.

trapezoid.why: SAOL carries TWO homographs with DIFFERENT genders: '1trapets [trapet´s] substantiv ~en ~er' glossed 'ett gymnastikredskap' (the gymnastics trapeze = EN-ord), and '2trapets [trapet´s] substantiv ~et ~er' glossed 'parallelltrapets' (the GEOMETRIC figure = ETT-ord). The picture is a bare geometric quadrilateral in the 'shapes' theme, i.e. sense 2 → ~et → neuter → t. The stored 'n' is the wrong homograph: it makes a maths shape into a circus apparatus. 'Ett trapets' is the correct form to read aloud beside this picture.

us.why: USA is NEUTER in Swedish. Both independent Wiktionary editions agree — sv.wiktionary: 'Böjningar av USA neutrum'; en.wiktionary Swedish section: 'USA n' — which is exactly the two-editions-agreeing standard the brief sets for cross-check evidence. It also follows the general Swedish rule that country/place names take neuter agreement ('USA är stort', 'Sverige är stort'; I verified sv.wiktionary marks Sverige neutrum too, as a control). SAOL/SO carry no proper nouns — stated, not fabricated. The stored 'n' is wrong. Contrast the sibling 'uncle-sam' row, which correctly stays n because a PERSON name keeps common gender: the two must not be aligned to each other.
